Maria: Quick Q — booking a dev summit in Berlin next month. Im planning to take the daytime train from Paris -> Berlin. The ticket PDF is a single combined invoice without itemized legs. Do we require itemized legs for rail to expense, or is a payment confirmation + itinerary screenshot okay?

Raj: You can expense rail travel. For EU rail we need either an itemized receipt OR a combination of (a) booking/itinerary screenshot showing train numbers/dates/times and (b) payment confirmation showing the amount. If the invoice is a bundled PDF, attach both.

Lina: If Im on a personal season pass and only pay an incremental surcharge for a high-speed train, how should I submit that?

Raj: Good question. Reimburse the incremental surcharge only. Upload the surcharge receipt and include a short note like: "used season pass, reimbursing surcharge". Also attach a screenshot of your season pass if available.

Omar: Conference registrations often include lunches. How does that affect per diem? Example: two conference lunches already paid in the registration.

Maria: Per diem is prorated. Deduct meals included in registration from the daily per diem. Attach the conference agenda/registration confirmation that explicitly lists which meals are included.

Lina: Any guidance on class for long rail rides? 2nd vs 1st vs sleeper?

Raj: Policy highlights: up to ~4h — 2nd class/standard. Over ~4h you may book 1st class for work that needs rest/productivity, but get manager approval if >€100 upgrade. Sleeper/overnight berths allowed when the total cost (ticket + berth) is cheaper than flight+hotel. For any exception >€200, require manager pre-approval in the expense.

Maria: Also — do receipts need translation? Many German/French rail receipts are not in English.

Raj: Non-English receipts are fine. Finance accepts originals + a short English summary in the expense notes. If using Expensify, paste the summary into the "Notes" field.

Lina: What if I booked with loyalty points and only paid taxes/fees? Do I claim the cash equivalent?

Raj: If you used points and paid only taxes/fees, you can claim the taxes/fees portion. If the booking was entirely covered by points with no cash outlay, it's not reimbursable. If you bought a refundable fare and later used points/credits, attach the card statement showing the original purchase or fees.

Maria: I'll draft a short checklist to add to the travel page. Draft checklist will include:
```
1) Booking confirmation (itinerary with train numbers/dates/times)
2) Payment confirmation or card statement showing amount paid
3) If using season pass/points: proof + short note about surcharge or fees
4) Conference agenda/registration (to show included meals)
5) English summary for non-English receipts
6) Manager pre-approval for exceptions >€200 or for 1st-class upgrades over policy
```

Raj: Nice. Ping me on the draft and Ill double-check wording for Finance. :+1:
